location: src/haute/_ast_helpers.py:203-231 (_strip_docstring), specifically the single-line branch at :219-221 (`if stripped.count(opening_quote) >= 2 and stripped.endswith(opening_quote)`) and the close test at :215
title: _strip_docstring swallows the entire function body when a single-line docstring has a trailing comment after the closing triple-quote
description: When a function's docstring is a single-line triple-quoted string followed by a trailing comment on the same line (e.g. `"""Doc."""  # note`), `_strip_docstring` discards the docstring AND every subsequent line of the body, returning only the docstring's leading whitespace lines (effectively []). This is valid Python and `ast.get_docstring` recognises it as the docstring, so the body the heuristic is meant to preserve (`x = 1; return x`, etc.) is silently lost. The single-line fast-path at :221 requires `stripped.endswith(opening_quote)`; with a trailing comment the line ends with the comment text, not `"""`, so the `else` branch sets `in_docstring = True`. From then on, line 215 looks for a line that *contains* `opening_quote`, but the only such line was the (now consumed) opener, so the loop `continue`s past every remaining body line (line 218) without ever appending them. This corrupts the extracted user code that `_code_extraction._extract_user_code` (src/haute/_code_extraction.py:964) persists into the node config box, so a round-trip (parse -> codegen) drops the user's logic. This is DISTINCT from known finding #4: that finding was about mixed/embedded triple-quote runs *inside* a multi-line docstring body and was REFUTED by review/03-simplification/repro/parser__NEWBUG-03.py (its 10 valid-Python cases all matched the AST oracle); none of them placed a comment or any content after the closing quote on the docstring's own line. A second, rarer variant of the same root cause: a first statement that is a triple-quoted string *concatenation/BinOp* (e.g. `"""a""" + foo`) is NOT a docstring per ast, yet _strip_docstring treats the opener line as a docstring start and swallows the statement plus all following lines.
evidence:
Source: `def f():
    """Doc."""  # trailing comment
    x = 1
    return x`. ast.get_docstring(func) == 'Doc.' and func.body[0] is an Expr (a real docstring). _extract_function_bodies(...)['f'] == '    """Doc."""  # trailing comment
    x = 1
    return x'. _strip_docstring(body.splitlines()) == [] (verified by running it in the project venv). AST ground truth (ast.get_docstring + docstring node end_lineno, the same oracle used by parser__NEWBUG-03.py) keeps ['x = 1', 'return x']; _strip_docstring returns [] -> AGREE: False. No existing test in tests/test_parser_internals.py::TestStripDocstring or tests/test_parser_helpers.py covers a trailing comment after the closing quote.
behavior_preservation: The behavior-preserving fix is to derive the docstring boundary from the AST (ast.get_docstring + func.body[0].end_lineno) — already available because the parser passes the parsed tree into _extract_function_bodies — instead of the line-scanning heuristic; this also subsumes known finding #4's concern.
